description: QURA TEAM — команда разработчиков из Алматы на NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. Мы создаем функциональные веб-сервисы, интерактивные интерфейсы и AI-решения на основе открытых данных NASA.
summary:
AGRONA is a web-based agricultural decision-support platform that transforms NASA Earth observation data into explainable crop rotation strategies.

Farmers face a complex challenge: choosing what to grow next while considering soil health, water availability, climate conditions, and previous crops. Repeated cultivation of similar crops can increase soil nutrient depletion and agronomic risks, while changing weather patterns make long-term planning more difficult.

We developed a working application where farmers can draw their field boundaries on an interactive map, save crop histories, analyze environmental conditions, and compare multi-season crop rotation strategies.

AGRONA integrates NASA POWER climate data to assess temperature, precipitation, humidity, wind, solar radiation, dry spells, and temperature-related risks. We also implemented NASA HLS satellite data processing to support vegetation analysis.

Our explainable recommendation engine combines soil, water, and climate factors using weighted multi-criteria scoring and Beam Search, retaining up to 24 candidate sequences at each step.

The prototype has passed 120 automated tests, completed 12 NASA POWER processing jobs, and successfully executed a year-long NASA HLS processing job.

AGRONA helps turn complex environmental observations into practical, transparent agricultural decisions.
details:
AGRONA — Project Details

1. Project Overview

AGRONA is a web-based agricultural decision-support platform developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026: Field Shift — Adapting Farms with NASA Data.

Our goal is to bridge the gap between Earth observation data and practical agricultural decisions.

Instead of providing generic weather information, AGRONA connects geographic field boundaries, historical crop information, environmental observations, and an explainable crop rotation planning algorithm.

The result is a platform designed to help farmers evaluate different crop rotation strategies while considering climate suitability, water requirements, and soil-related agronomic risks.

2. The Problem We Address

Farmers must make planting decisions under several interconnected constraints.

Soil health: Repeated cultivation of the same crop or crop family can contribute to nutrient depletion and increase pest and disease risks.

Climate variability: Temperature fluctuations, extreme heat, frost events, and changing growing-season conditions make crop selection more challenging.

Water availability: Irregular precipitation and extended dry periods increase uncertainty about whether a crop can complete its growing cycle.

Information fragmentation: Environmental information exists across multiple datasets, but translating these observations into field-level decisions remains difficult.

Our central question was:

How can we help a farmer choose a sequence of crops for future seasons using their field history and NASA environmental data?

3. What We Built

We developed a working web application with several connected components.

Interactive Field Mapping

AGRONA allows users to identify and draw agricultural field boundaries on an interactive geographic map.

The application works with geographic polygons representing actual field locations.

Users can save fields and reuse their information in subsequent analyses.

Crop History Management

Farmers can record crops previously cultivated on their fields.

This historical information provides context for evaluating future crop rotation options.

Instead of treating every planting season independently, AGRONA considers the relationship between previous and potential future crops.

Climate Analysis

AGRONA integrates NASA POWER as its operational climate data source.

The system processes environmental observations associated with the selected field.

These observations include:

  • Air temperature
  • Precipitation
  • Relative humidity
  • Wind conditions
  • Solar radiation

The data support climate suitability scoring, dry-spell detection, and temperature-related risk analysis.

For example, during one field analysis, AGRONA identified a continuous 14-day period with daily precipitation below 1 mm.

This demonstrates how environmental measurements can be transformed into understandable agricultural risk indicators.

Satellite Data Processing

We also implemented a processing workflow using NASA Harmonized Landsat and Sentinel-2 (HLS) observations.

A year-long HLS processing job was successfully completed.

This provides a technical foundation for incorporating vegetation observations into future field-level analysis and validation workflows.

Crop Rotation Planning

AGRONA includes an explainable crop rotation engine designed to compare different multi-season planting strategies.

The engine evaluates candidate sequences using three main categories:

Soil + Water + Climate

It combines multiple criteria through a weighted scoring approach.

To search through possible crop sequences, we implemented Beam Search.

At each step, the algorithm retains up to 24 promising candidates for further evaluation.

This approach allows the system to explore multi-season crop sequences without exhaustively evaluating every possible combination.

AGRONA presents a baseline strategy alongside up to two distinct alternatives.

Users can examine the proposed crop sequences, compare relevant considerations, and review explanations of potential benefits, limitations, and risks.

4. Our Technical Approach

Our development focused on connecting several components into a coherent decision-support workflow.

Step 1 — Geographic input

The user selects or draws a field boundary.

Step 2 — Agricultural context

The user records previous crops and relevant field information.

Step 3 — Environmental data processing

NASA POWER observations are processed to generate climate indicators and risk signals.

Step 4 — Candidate evaluation

The rotation engine evaluates potential crop sequences using weighted soil, water, and climate criteria.

Step 5 — Search and comparison

Beam Search retains promising candidates and supports comparison of the baseline strategy with alternative rotations.

Step 6 — Explainable output

The application presents candidate rotations with supporting explanations and identified risks.

This workflow connects Earth observation data to an understandable agricultural planning process.

5. NASA Data and Resources

NASA POWER

NASA POWER is our core operational climate data source.

It supports analysis of meteorological and agroclimatic variables used in field-level assessments.

NASA HLS

NASA Harmonized Landsat and Sentinel-2 observations support satellite vegetation data processing.

Our project successfully completed a year-long HLS processing job.

Additional Resources Explored

We investigated other NASA Earth observation datasets, including GPM IMERG, SMAP, ECOSTRESS, MODIS, VIIRS, SRTM, GLDAS, and NLDAS.

These resources offer opportunities to extend environmental analysis, including precipitation, soil moisture, land surface temperature, vegetation conditions, and terrain characteristics.

However, NASA POWER remains our operational climate input, and other integrations have different levels of readiness.

6. Engineering Results

AGRONA is a working minimum viable product rather than a presentation-only concept.

Our development and verification results include:

120 automated tests passed

  • 95 frontend tests
  • 25 Python tests

12 NASA POWER processing jobs completed

These jobs were successfully completed and recorded in the database.

1 successful year-long NASA HLS processing job

This demonstrates progress toward incorporating satellite vegetation observations into the application.

These results provide measurable evidence of software development, data processing, and technical verification.

7. What Makes AGRONA Different?

AGRONA is designed around the connection between environmental evidence and multi-season agricultural planning.

Its distinguishing features include:

Field-specific workflows: Users work with actual geographic field boundaries rather than generic regional selections.

Historical crop context: Previous crops are included when exploring future rotations.

NASA-powered climate analysis: Environmental observations contribute to agricultural risk assessment.

Multi-season planning: The system compares crop sequences rather than recommending only a single crop.

Explainable recommendations: Users can examine alternatives, criteria, limitations, and potential trade-offs.

Technical verification: The prototype includes automated testing and completed environmental data processing jobs.

8. Intended Impact

AGRONA is designed to make scientific environmental information more accessible to farmers.

For farmers, the platform offers a structured way to explore crop rotation options based on their field history and environmental conditions.

For agricultural sustainability, it may support better-informed decisions concerning soil health, water requirements, and climate adaptation.

For scientific transparency, AGRONA emphasizes understandable indicators, documented data sources, and reproducible computational approaches.

Our system is intended to support farmers and agricultural specialists, not replace their professional judgment.

9. Current Limitations and Future Development

Our next development priorities include restoring the SoilGrids API integration, validating the complete farmer workflow, and improving the reliability of the NASA HLS processing queue.

We also plan to strengthen field-level validation and evaluate the practical usefulness of crop rotation recommendations.

We do not claim verified increases in crop yield or quantified water savings at this stage.

Our current achievement is a working, technically tested decision-support prototype with operational NASA climate data processing and an explainable crop rotation engine.

10. Conclusion

AGRONA demonstrates how NASA Earth observation data can be connected with agricultural field histories and explainable algorithms to support better farming decisions.

Our vision is to make advanced environmental information useful at the level where farmers make their most important decisions: the field.

Satellites observe the Earth. AGRONA helps farmers decide.
